description: holon-coherence keeps exactly three append-only ledgers (intents, plans, executions) under holon-knowledge/ledger. Nothing checks that no fourth ledger-like store appears, nor that rows already on the base branch stay byte-identical on a pull request head.
goal: Add two standalone checks and run them from a new CI workflow on pull requests. A store check scripts/check_ledger_stores.py lists the jsonl ledger stores under holon-knowledge and fails when the set is anything other than intents.jsonl, plans.jsonl and executions.jsonl (any other jsonl file outside holon-knowledge/kb fails). A diff check scripts/check_ledger_rows_append_only.py compares every ledger file on the base branch with the head and fails when a base row changed, moved or disappeared; added rows pass, and an unreadable base fails closed. Each script has importable functions and a command-line entry point with --base and --head. Code is self-explaining: no docstrings and no comments except '# why:' comments that record a reason the code cannot show.
rationale: The ledgers are the audit trail; a fourth store or an edited row breaks the audit invariant silently, and only a machine check keeps it from slipping through.
acceptance_criteria: Hygiene test: the set of ledger stores (files/dirs matching the ledger layout, and any new `*.jsonl` ledger-like file outside the KB) equals exactly those three: tests/test_ledger_stores_exactly_three.py builds a temporary repository with a fourth jsonl ledger-like file and proves scripts/check_ledger_stores.py fails, and proves the real repository layout passes.

CI diff check: in a PR, ledger rows present on the base are byte-identical on the head (append-only); fragments only add: tests/test_ledger_rows_append_only_diff.py proves on a hermetic git repository that scripts/check_ledger_rows_append_only.py fails when a base row is edited, deleted or reordered, passes when rows are only added, and fails closed when the base is unreadable.
.github/workflows/test-ledger-invariants.yml runs both scripts on pull requests; the workflow file is new and no existing workflow file is edited.
Hygiene test: the set of ledger stores (files/dirs matching the ledger layout, and any new `*.jsonl` ledger-like file outside the KB) equals exactly those three.
CI diff check: in a PR, ledger rows present on the base are byte-identical on the head (append-only); fragments only add.
The check runs automatically (pre-commit hook and/or CI, and the flow gate where it applies); no agent has to remember it.
The check is proven to fail on a real or reconstructed violation (a test with today's evidence) before it is trusted, and passes on the cleaned state.
Self-explaining code invariant in anything written: no docstrings, no comments except `# why:`.
Target-repository work goes through `holon flow`; the intent never names harness paths or bean ids.
Every new module is at most 200 lines; the module budget configuration is unchanged; the project's pytest and lint tasks pass.
